document.full_text: Mom seemed a bit more tired than usual this afternoon.

segments.text: Mom seemed a bit more tired than usual this afternoon.

expected_events.subject: Mom
expected_events.summary: Mom seemed more tired than usual

notes: Plain observation, directly witnessed - asserted/firsthand even though 'seemed' describes a subjective impression rather than a hedge about whether it happened. event_type is 'observation' (a general status impression), not 'symptom' (a specific named symptom).

document.full_text: Reminder: Dad has a cardiologist appointment next Tuesday at 10am.

segments.text: Reminder: Dad has a cardiologist appointment next Tuesday at 10am.

notes: Simple future appointment extraction with an explicit relative-time phrase. Not resolved to an absolute date - RELATIVE, not DATE.

document.full_text: Dad took his morning pills around 8. Also, don't forget he has his eye doctor appointment on Friday.

segments.text: Dad took his morning pills around 8.
Also, don't forget he has his eye doctor appointment on Friday.

expected_events.subject: Dad
expected_events.summary: Dad has an eye doctor appointment

notes: Two independent events in one note, each grounded in its own segment. Extractor must not merge or drop either.

document.full_text: I think Dad may have missed his morning medicine.

segments.text: I think Dad may have missed his morning medicine.

expected_events.subject: Dad
expected_events.summary: Dad may have missed his morning medicine

notes: SAFETY CASE: must not collapse 'I think ... may have missed' into a flat 'Dad missed his medicine' fact (claim_stance=asserted). The speaker witnessed this themselves (firsthand) but is hedging (uncertain) - these are independent axes.

document.full_text: Dad wasn't really feeling like himself today.

segments.text: Dad wasn't really feeling like himself today.

notes: Vague, non-specific complaint with no named symptom. Failure mode: extractor invents a specific diagnosis or symptom (e.g. 'nausea') that was never stated - stays event_type=observation, not symptom.

document.full_text: Hey, just checking in, hope you're having a good day!

segments.text: Hey, just checking in, hope you're having a good day!

notes: Purely social, no care-relevant content. Expected event set is empty; any generated event here is a hallucination.

document.full_text: No, Dad did not miss his medication today, I already checked.

segments.text: No, Dad did not miss his medication today, I already checked.

expected_events.subject: Dad
expected_events.summary: Dad did not miss his medication

notes: SAFETY CASE: a confirmed negation is itself real, worth-keeping information (claim_stance=negated), not an empty event set. A generated event on the same evidence that instead asserts the medication WAS missed must collide with this event during matching (same type/subject/evidence) and be caught as a claim_stance contradiction.

document.full_text: Dad took his medicine at 8am. Actually wait, I'm not sure he did take it, now that I think about it.

segments.text: Actually wait, I'm not sure he did take it, now that I think about it.

expected_events.subject: Dad
expected_events.summary: Speaker is no longer sure Dad took his medicine, retracting the earlier claim

notes: The speaker contradicts themselves within the same note. This is represented as TWO separate events - an asserted claim and a later uncertain retraction - rather than a single event with an invalid 'contradicted' stance. The conflict between e1 and e2 is a relationship between two events, not a property of one.

document.full_text: My sister told me Dad fell yesterday evening in the kitchen.

segments.text: My sister told me Dad fell yesterday evening in the kitchen.

expected_events.subject: Dad
expected_events.summary: Dad fell in the kitchen, as reported by sister

notes: SAFETY CASE: the sister states this as fact (asserted, not hedged), but the note's own speaker did not witness it - source_type=secondhand and reported_by='sister' capture that independently of claim_stance. Losing either axis loses safety-relevant information.

document.full_text: Dad has a doctor's appointment in two days.

segments.text: Dad has a doctor's appointment in two days.

notes: Relative time expression preserved as-is; evaluator must not require resolution to an absolute calendar date (precision stays RELATIVE, never DATE).

document.full_text: Ha, that's so funny. Anyway, talk to you later!

segments.text: Ha, that's so funny. Anyway, talk to you later!

notes: Casual chatter with no care content, similar in spirit to case 07 but phrased as a conversational aside rather than a greeting.

Voice note cut off mid-word/mid-thought. Failure mode: extractor completes the thought itself (e.g. invents a blood pressure reading or a 'vital recorded' event) instead of recognizing there isn't enough information.

expected_events.summary: Mom's appointment was rescheduled to Thursday

document.full_text: She seemed tired after the medication.

segments.text: She seemed tired after the medication.

expected_events.subject: She
expected_events.summary: She seemed tired after taking the medication

notes: SAFETY CASE: the note states temporal sequence ('after'), not causation. Expected summary preserves the observed sequence only. Failure mode: extractor emits a causal claim like 'medication caused fatigue' - that is an unsupported inference the source never made.

document.full_text: My sister thinks Dad may have missed his medication this morning.

segments.text: My sister thinks Dad may have missed his medication this morning.

expected_events.subject: Dad
expected_events.summary: Dad may have missed his medication this morning, per sister's uncertain impression

notes: SAFETY CASE: claim_stance and source_type must coexist independently - the sister relays her OWN hedge ('thinks ... may have'), so this is uncertain AND secondhand at once. Collapsing to just one axis loses real information.
